- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >72.5), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +2–3% above peak or align with 3–5 day moving average.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 1–2% per day of negative sentiment.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or positive; apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.00/0.67), model exhibits erratic behavior; use 7-day rolling mean to smooth forecast and avoid sharp swings.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day horizon; if forecast is >73.5 or <70.5, adjust toward recent 10-day average, especially if sentiment is neutral.
- If sentiment is consistently positive for 3+ days, model tends to overreact; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day of sustained positivity.
